Company: SkyHop Airlines

US regional airline (~3,500 employees) flying short domestic routes from hubs in Denver and Salt Lake City. Fleet is 60 Embraer E175 jets and 25 Airbus A320-family jets (A319 and A320). Sells tickets online and at airports, charges bag fees, and runs its own maintenance hangar. Does not fly Boeing aircraft, Airbus A220/A350, or helicopters; no cargo-only flights, no international routes.

Rules that APPLY:
- FAA airworthiness directives for Embraer E175 (ERJ 170 family) or Airbus A319/A320, and their engines
- FAA rules for airline operations, pilots, crew rest and drug/alcohol testing
- DOT consumer rules for airline passengers (refunds, fees, accessibility)
- Airspace or airport rules at Denver or Salt Lake City, and airport fees charged to passengers
- TSA security rules for airlines

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Airworthiness directives for aircraft models we do not fly (Boeing, A220, A350, business jets, small planes, helicopters)
- Airspace changes at airports we do not serve
- Commercial space launches, drones, air-traffic-control equipment
- Banking, food, pharmacy, energy

[2026-22576] Rule — Environmental Protection Agency
Title: Significant New Use Rules on Certain Chemical Substances (25-3.5e)
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: EPA is issuing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances that were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and are also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. The SNURs require persons to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing the manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of any of these chemical substances for an activity that is designated as a significant new use in the SNUR. [2026-22587] Proposed Rule — Transportation Department; Federal Aviation Administration
Title: Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes
Action: Notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM).
Abstract: The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain Airbus SAS Model A318-111 and -112 airplanes; Model A319- 111, -112, -113, -114, -115, -131, -132, and -133 airplanes; Model A320-211, -212, -214, -216, -231, -232, and -233 airplanes; and Model A321-111, -112, -131, -211, -212, -213, -231, and -232 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of damage to the YZ-axis attachment points on airplanes equipped with certain overhead stowage compartments (OHSC) bins. Investigations showed that bushings, retainer rings, and pins had migrated from their original positions. This proposed AD would require a one-time inspection for discrepancies of affected OHSC bins and, depending on findings, accomplishment of applicable corrective actions. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected parts. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

[2026-22717] Rule — Justice Department; Drug Enforcement Administration
Title: Specific Listing for 3-Chloromethcathinone, A Currently Controlled Schedule I Substance
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) is establishing a specific listing and DEA Controlled Substances Code Number (drug code) for 1-(3-chlorophenyl)-2-(methylamino)propan-1-one (3- chloromethcathinone; 3-CMC) in schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act (CSA). Although 3-chloromethcathinone is not specifically listed in schedule I of the CSA with its own unique drug code, it is a schedule I controlled substances in the United States because it is a positional isomer of 4-chloromethcathinone, which is a schedule I hallucinogen. Therefore, DEA is simply amending the schedule I hallucinogenic substances list in its regulations to separately include 3- chloromethcathinone.

Title: Conforming Amendment Regarding the Criminal Law Technical Amendments Act of 2002
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The Criminal Law Technical Amendments Act of 2002 ("Technical Amendments Act") became law on November 2, 2002, as part of the 21st Century Department of Justice Appropriations Authorization Act. Title: Improving Transparency Into Pharmacy Benefit Manager Fee Disclosure

Abstract: The Department is issuing a final regulation that will require providers of pharmacy benefit management services and affiliated providers of brokerage and consulting services to disclose information about their compensation to fiduciaries of large, self-insured group health plans subject to the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA). Pharmacy spending is a major driver of overall healthcare costs for employers and is growing faster than medical and surgical spending. These disclosure requirements apply for purposes of ERISA's statutory prohibited transaction exemption for service arrangements under section 408(b)(2). [2026-22380] Rule — Health and Human Services Department; Office of the Secretary
Title: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance
Action: Final rule.
Abstract: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS or Department) issues this rule to revise the regulation implementing section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 (section 504) as it applies to recipients of HHS funding (entitled "Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Disability in Programs or Activities Receiving Federal Financial Assistance," ("2024 Final Rule")), published on May 9, 2024. This rule clarifies that the Department interprets the statutory exclusion of "gender identity disorders not resulting from physical impairments" from the terms "individual with a disability" and "disability" set forth in our regulations to encompass "gender dysphoria not resulting from a physical impairment" for purposes of the regulation. This clarification is necessary to resolve ambiguity introduced in the preamble to the 2024 Final Rule and to ensure compliance with the best reading of the governing statute.

[2026-22450] Proposed Rule — Transportation Department; Federal Aviation Administration
Title: Update and Clarification of the Passenger Facility Charge Regulations
Action: Supplemental notice of proposed rulemaking (SNPRM).
Abstract: On September 27, 2023 FAA published a notice of proposed rulemaking (NPRM) to amend its Passenger Facility Charge (PFC) regulations to implement congressionally mandated changes to an existing pilot program within the PFC program. FAA also proposed to reaffirm existing program requirements and update or remove obsolete references within the PFC regulations. Following publication of the NPRM and before FAA issued a final rule, the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024 (the 2024 Act) was signed into law on May 16, 2024. Several sections of the 2024 Act necessitate changes to PFC regulations or modifications to proposals made in the NPRM. As such, FAA now issues this supplemental proposal addressing: PFC turnback reductions; two new PFC-eligible projects; restrictions to PFC-eligible projects; FAA's timeline for review and acknowledgement of notice of intent (NOI) submissions; PFC streamlining review eligibility; and PFC submittal requirements. This proposal aligns with the requirements established by the 2024 Act.
